title: Scaling & Architecture
blurb: Why models got bigger, what the scaling laws actually said, and how anyone trains something that no longer fits on a GPU.

anchors.note: The architecture everything else in this list is built on.
Loss falls as a power law in compute, data and parameters. The paper that made scaling a plan rather than a hope.
Few-shot behaviour emerging from scale alone. The empirical shock that set the agenda.
Corrects the earlier scaling laws: most large models were badly undertrained on data. Changed how everyone allocates compute.
Tensor parallelism — how to split a single layer across GPUs.
Shards optimiser state, gradients and parameters. The memory arithmetic behind most large-scale training.
Mixture of experts with a single expert per token, making trillion-parameter models trainable.
A sparse MoE that was genuinely good and openly released. Made MoE a practical choice rather than a curiosity.
